Anika (AcmeMaps): Hey, support — we're seeing a flurry of duplicate completions after our clients reconnect to the streaming SSE endpoint. Usage spiked and billing page shows many extra tokens. Can share logs.
Maya (Support): ack, sorry you're hitting this. Quick question: are you using our JS SDK or a custom SSE client?
Anika (AcmeMaps): custom SSE client running in mobile webviews. We reconnect on 'close' and try to resume. Client sends a session_id but sometimes no resume_token.
Maya (Support): got it. Can you paste a minimal repro (headers + small timeline)?
Anika (AcmeMaps): timeline: connect -> partial chunk (seq 37) -> disconnect -> reconnect within 800ms -> request includes session_id but no resume_token -> server streams chunk for seq 37 again and then continues -> client now has duplicate text and we bill for both. Logs: ```
[2026-02-18T21:12:07.453Z] conn_open session=acme-123 req_id=rid-9c4
[2026-02-18T21:12:08.120Z] sse_send event=chunk id=seq-37 data={"text":"...partial...","seq":37}
[2026-02-18T21:12:09.001Z] conn_close session=acme-123 req_id=rid-9c4 reason=network
[2026-02-18T21:12:09.879Z] conn_open session=acme-123 req_id=rid-9c5
[2026-02-18T21:12:09.880Z] request headers: Authorization=Bearer <redacted>, X-Session-Id=acme-123, X-Resume-Token= (missing)
[2026-02-18T21:12:09.881Z] sse_send event=chunk id=seq-37 data={"text":"...partial...","seq":37} // duplicate
```
Derek (SRE): thanks — that log snippet is super helpful. Two quick hypotheses: 1) server treats missing resume token as new stream and re-emits last buffered chunks; 2) client-side race where reconnect arrives before resume token is fetched and sent. Both can create duplicate billing.
Maya (Support): @Derek any known safety net on server for at-most-once delivery? We should also check whether request-id dedup is enforced across reconnects.
Derek (SRE): currently server dedupe keys are tied to `idempotency-key` header if present. For streaming resume we rely on `resume_token` + seq numbers. If resume_token is absent, we fall back to resending last emitted buffer to avoid gaps. That behavior was chosen to prioritize continuity over duplicates.
Josh (Infra): FYI the fallback resend behavior is in runtime v3.2. We introduced it to avoid truncated outputs for stateless clients. But agree it creates duplicate billing in some edge cases.
Anika (AcmeMaps): is there a short-term mitigation? Customers are asking for refunds now.
Maya (Support): immediate mitigation options: 1) we can issue a temporary usage credit while we investigate, 2) ask you to enforce client-side de-dupe by ignoring repeated seq numbers, or 3) toggle server-side conservative mode (no resend if resume_token missing) for your org while we implement dedupe. Which is easiest for you?
Anika (AcmeMaps): toggling server-side is best, but we need it fast.
AlertBot: New incident created INC-2026-432: sse-dup-completions-acme-123 (priority: P2).
Derek (SRE): I'll open a config flip for acme org to set `sse.strict_resume=true` which will avoid resending the last chunk when resume_token is missing. That reduces duplicates but risks short gaps for buggy clients.
Derek (SRE): plan: 1) flip `sse.strict_resume` for acme-123 (try on a single-host canary) 2) add server-side dedupe layer keyed by (session_id, seq) for 24h 3) add telemetry to surface reconnects missing resume_token 4) coordinate billing team for credits.
Maya (Support): Derek can you paste the canary command? Anika, we'll need a small maintenance window ~5m to flip.
Derek (SRE): canary command (internal): ```
POST /internal/configs/orgs/acme-123
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "sse.strict_resume": true,
  "who": "derek"
}
```
Maya (Support): Anika do you want us to proceed with the flip + provisional credit?
Anika (AcmeMaps): yes please proceed with both. Also our devs will push a client patch to send resume_token immediately on reconnect. ETA 48h.
Josh (Infra): follow-ups for eng-runtime: please consider adding a soft dedupe period on token/seq for streaming to avoid charging twice. We should also add a metric `reconnect.missing_resume_token_rate`.
Derek (SRE): created internal ticket RINF-2047 for dedupe implementation and telemetry. Linking to incident: INC-2026-432.
Maya (Support): Billing note: @billing-team we'll need to reconcile tokens billed between 21:12:07 and 21:18:00 for acme-123. Requesting manual credit for obvious duplicates until dedupe is live.
Anika (AcmeMaps): added a few more traces from client showing where resume_token fetch can stall: ```
// client pseudocode
onclose -> setTimeout(reconnect, 200) // resumes rely on async token refresh
async reconnect() {
  let token = await fetchResumeToken(); // can reject on flakey network
  open_sse({ session_id, resume_token: token });
}
```
Maya (Support): perfect, that matches the races we suspected. Short-term advice for clients: 1) include `idempotency-key` on the initial create-completion request, 2) if resume_token unavailable, delay reconnect slightly and exponential backoff, 3) dedupe on seq numbers on client.
Derek (SRE): operational checklist for us: - flip config on canary - monitor error/dup metrics - prepare rollback - implement server dedupe (RINF-2047) - ensure billing chargeback UI is available for credits.
Maya (Support): Anika I'll open a billing credit request now and attach the logs you provided. Expect update in 2-4h. :bow:
Anika (AcmeMaps): thanks all. Please keep me posted in-thread. We'll ship client fix in ~48h and test strict_resume.
Derek (SRE): update 21:14 UTC: canary flip applied to host s-14. No immediate errors. Monitoring for duplicate seq emissions.
Maya (Support): update 21:18 UTC: billing ticket BT-789 opened and linked to INC-2026-432.
Josh (Infra): note for eng-runtime: if we implement dedupe, be explicit about retention window and limits so it doesn't become a state explosion for high-throughput streams.
Maya (Support): closing loop: estimated timeline: immediate credit + canary flip (now) -> dedupe rollout (2-3 weeks) -> client fix (customer 48h). We'll follow up with postmortem once dedupe is deployed.
Anika (AcmeMaps): appreciated — thanks for the quick support team.
Derek (SRE): adding a tiny TODO: add a server header `X-Resume-Required: true|false` to make the server intent explicit for clients (followup RINF-2050).
Maya (Support): noted. I'll create a short KB article describing safe reconnect semantics and recommended client patterns (de-dupe on seq, send resume_token, idempotency-key).
Anika (AcmeMaps): ok logging off for today. Please put final notes in the incident.
